answer.rationale: Competitive pricing pressure creates immediate temptation to match discounts, but exp_73 evidence is clear: targeted SMB discounting acquired cohorts that did not survive renewal, contradicting the primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Promotional_pricing is a short-term defensive trap that compounds retention problems. Instead, activate three proven levers in sequence: (1) Activation_messaging (memory_91) has directly improved week-one engagement and nudged accounts to first meaningful action—critical for price-sensitive buyers who need to experience product value before renewal decisions. (2) Simplify_onboarding (memory_31) and shorten onboarding (memory_86) reduce friction and accelerate time-to-value, addressing the core vulnerability of price-sensitive segments: they defect when they don't see value quickly. (3) For accounts showing churn signal, referral_incentive (memory_57) provides a retention and expansion lever that works on established customers without requiring discount capitulation. A small_guarded_test of activation_messaging + onboarding simplification for at-risk SMB cohorts preserves the option to escalate to sales_assist or referral programs if needed, while avoiding the durability cliff that deep discounting creates. This directly addresses why they're churning (lack of perceived value) rather than why they're price-sensitive (commoditized positioning). The uncertainty preserved: we do not yet know if activation velocity alone can retain this specific cohort under competitive pressure, nor whether a hybrid approach (messaging + referral incentive) would be more effective. Small test allows learning before broader commitment.
